findings.name: The local lazy loader still ignores independent vector-oracle certification
findings.scope: uncommitted lazy promotion; not a shipped main fetch path
findings.detail: The local loader verifies digest, exact bytes, identity, domain and declared caps, then freezes/caches the model. Deleting the certificate or raising its maxima to 1e9 and recomputing the shard digest/manifest remains admissible by inspection. The same old-local parser also retains the endpoint gap. Local generation checks real vector-oracle errors before publication, so this is a missing runtime semantic rejection boundary rather than proof of invalid current numerical fits.

findings.name: Early rejected lazy responses can outlive the concurrency permit
findings.detail: HTTP status and invalid/oversized Content-Length branches throw before acquiring a reader and never cancel response.body. withSlot releases or transfers the concurrency permit on rejection. Sequential failures can therefore leave body transfers active outside the configured accounting. Only the decoded-stream-overflow branch calls reader.cancel().
findings.targetedTestStatus: Existing local tests assert rejection and count fetch invocations, not stream cancellation before permit release. The historical controlled Response/ReadableStream probe recorded 3 transfers and 0 cancellations with concurrency=1; this is not a fresh deployed socket measurement.
findings.remaining: Cancel/abort every early rejected response before releasing its permit; assert cleanup for non-OK status and malformed/oversized advertised length with repeated loads.
